data: Front left corner of a large, well finished block of compact grey limestone. Broken to the rear, left and right sides in a diagonal break from mid-front to rear left coner. Intact top, bottom, front left. The lower face is finished smooth, like the front; The upper and left side faces are finished, but left rough picked.
Three lines of large Greek letters; all are incomplete, but the unjustified left margin suggests a text that was originally centred on the stone

Thinly incised broad letters of regular height, without serifs or marked terminations to the strokes. Alpha has straight bar; Beta has closed loops, in the second instance separated from one another. Sigma has parallel top and bottom strokes, the mid-strokes meeting slightly over halfway across.
Letters of the 3rd century BCE; the apparent double kingship reference suggests the Hieronian period

Found in foundation works for post office, c.1959, between via Eumelo, via Archia, and via Carabelli, together with ISic003427. Currently lying on the ground near the exit gate to the area of the amphitheatre in the archaeological park of Neapolis.

English translation

Jonathan Prag

To Damater and Kore

commentary

The text is speculatively restored in several different ways by previous editors: the primary difference being whether the dedicants are thought to be the royal individual named in line 2 (and perhaps also three, if not a filiation) (so Gentili, Dimartino), or whether the royal name in line 2 is instead the honorand in the accusative, with the subject then named in a shorter (and smaller) line 4 (so Manganaro). It is notable that no editor has yet considered the possibility that the dedicant might be a queen (presumably Philistis wife of Hieron II), rather than Nereis, wife of Gelon), not a king, or even the king and queen jointly.
